subject: Hospitality
title: Passive Design Principles
description: A quick, practical guide to Passive Design Principles.

hook.text: Passive design uses building orientation, shading, and natural ventilation to reduce energy needs.

buildup.text: Orienting a hotel to maximize winter sun and minimize summer heat can cut cooling costs by 20–30% with zero technology investment.

discovery.text: Traditional buildings in hot climates used thick walls, courtyards, and wind towers centuries before air conditioning existed.

twist.text: Modern glass hotels in tropical climates are energy disasters—beautiful but requiring massive cooling.

climax.text: Hotels like the Parkroyal on Pickering in Singapore use sky gardens and green walls as passive cooling.

punchline.text: Face the right direction, shade the right walls. Passive design works with nature.

quiz.question: What is 'passive design' in architecture?
options: Using orientation, shading, and ventilation to reduce energy needs without mechanical systems
